instructions: Questions from the 2025/2026 continuous assessment (CA) CBT. Every answer is explained after you submit.

questions.text: Who was the first to observe a chromosome?
questions.explanation: Wilhelm Hofmeister drew chromosomes in dividing plant cells in the 1840s. Waldeyer only gave them their name, in 1888.

questions.text: In which forms can a ribosome exist?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are 70S in prokaryotes (and in mitochondria and chloroplasts) and 80S in the cytoplasm of eukaryotes.

questions.text: What is the typical range of a cell's size?
questions.explanation: Most cells fall between 1 and 100 µm: bacteria near the lower end, plant and animal cells near the upper end.

questions.text: Which of the following organelles is non-membrane bound?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are made of RNA and protein with no membrane. Lysosomes, peroxisomes and the ER are all enclosed by membranes.

questions.text: Which of the following is present in both eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Every cell makes proteins, so every cell has ribosomes. Mitochondria, a nuclear membrane and chloroplasts occur only in eukaryotes.

questions.text: Chlorophyll is primarily involved in which biological process?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs the light energy that drives photosynthesis.

questions.text: Which of the following stores food, water, and waste within a cell?
questions.explanation: Vacuoles are membrane-bound sacs that store food, water and waste.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the Independent Assortment of genes?
options: Alleles of different genes separate independently during gamete formation
Two alleles for a trait separate during meiosis
One allele is always dominant over the other
Genes are always inherited together if they are on the same chromosome
questions.explanation: Independent assortment says the alleles of different genes separate independently of each other during gamete formation. Two alleles of one gene separating is the law of segregation.

questions.text: Cytosol is defined as?
options: The solid protein filaments of the cell
The external coating of the cell wall
The internal space of the nucleus
The fluid portion of the cytoplasm, excluding organelles
questions.explanation: Cytosol is the fluid part of the cytoplasm only. Cytoplasm is the cytosol plus the organelles.

questions.text: The ripened ovary of a flower is known as the?
questions.explanation: After fertilization the ovary ripens into the fruit and the ovules become the seeds.

questions.text: The seed develops from which part of the plant?
questions.explanation: A seed develops from a fertilized ovule.

questions.text: The primary reproductive part of a plant is the?
questions.explanation: The flower carries the stamens and carpels, so it is the reproductive part of a flowering plant.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a chromatin-associated protein?
questions.explanation: Tubulin builds microtubules and spindle fibres. Histones, SMC proteins and HMG proteins all bind chromatin.

questions.text: What is the primary function of microvilli in cellular structures?
options: To facilitate cellular movement and locomotion
To increase the surface area for absorption and secretion
To protect the cell from external pathogens
To synthesize proteins for the plasma membrane
questions.explanation: Microvilli are finger-like folds of the membrane that enlarge the surface for absorption and secretion.

questions.text: The following are characteristic features of heterochromatin as opposed to euchromatin, except?
options: It is more densely packed and highly condensed
It is generally transcriptionally inactive (genes are "turned off")
It stains more lightly when viewed under a microscope
It is typically found at the periphery of the nucleus
questions.explanation: Heterochromatin is condensed, so it stains darkly. Light staining is a feature of euchromatin.

questions.text: Plants that complete their life cycle from germination to seed production over the course of two years are called?
questions.explanation: Biennials take two years: they grow in the first and flower and seed in the second.

questions.text: The primary function of a Histone is?
questions.explanation: DNA winds around histones, which packs it into chromosomes.

questions.text: The most conserved form of Histone across eukaryotic organisms is?
questions.explanation: H4 is almost identical across eukaryotes. H1 is the least conserved histone.

questions.text: Which of the following scientists provided evidence that refuted Jean Lamarck's theory of "inheritance of acquired traits"?
questions.explanation: August Weismann cut off mice's tails for many generations and the young were still born with tails, so acquired traits are not inherited.

questions.text: In a dihybrid cross (AaBb × AaBb), what is the fraction of offspring with the "Homozygous Dominant" genotype (AABB)?
questions.explanation: AA has a probability of 1/4 and BB has 1/4, so AABB is 1/4 × 1/4 = 1/16.

questions.text: In the biological study of a classroom ecosystem, which of the following is not typically observed?
questions.explanation: A classroom ecosystem study lists, collects and observes organisms. Artificial selection is breeding, not observation.

questions.text: The primary function of a Ribosome is?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes join amino acids together to make proteins.

questions.text: The cytoskeleton is primarily composed of?
questions.explanation: The cytoskeleton is a network of protein filaments: actin filaments, intermediate filaments and microtubules.

questions.text: The function of a Vacuole is most closely associated with?
options: Storage of water, nutrients, and waste
questions.explanation: Vacuoles store water, nutrients and waste. ATP comes from mitochondria.

questions.text: The Phospholipid Bilayer structure of the cell membrane is based on which scientific model?
questions.explanation: Singer and Nicolson's fluid mosaic model describes the membrane as a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it.

questions.text: The specialized protective caps at the end of chromosomes are called?
questions.explanation: Telomeres cap the ends of chromosomes and stop them wearing away or sticking together.

questions.text: Which of the following is lightly stained and transcriptionally active?
questions.explanation: Euchromatin is loosely packed, so it stains lightly and its genes can be transcribed.

questions.text: Reproduction, nutrition, and irritability (response to stimuli) are characteristics of?
questions.explanation: Reproduction, nutrition and irritability are characteristics of all living things, both animals and plants.

questions.text: Which of the following organisms belongs to Kingdom Plantae?
questions.explanation: A daisy is a flowering plant. Starfish and jellyfish are animals and a mushroom is a fungus.

questions.text: All the following are recognized types of chromosomes except?
questions.explanation: Autosomes, sex chromosomes and B-chromosomes (extra, non-essential ones) are recognised types. "C-chromosomes" are not.

questions.text: The protein complex that holds sister chromatids together after DNA replication until they are separated during mitosis is?
questions.explanation: Cohesin holds sister chromatids together until anaphase. Condensin compacts chromosomes.

questions.text: A flower that possesses only one type of reproductive organ is described as?
questions.explanation: A flower with only stamens or only carpels is unisexual. Dioecious describes a whole plant species, not a flower.

questions.text: A flower is scientifically described as "complete" if it possesses how many whorls?
questions.explanation: A complete flower has four whorls: calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium.

questions.text: What are the thread-like structures found in the nucleus that become visible during cell division?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes condense and become visible as threads during cell division.

questions.text: The core or internal structural arrangement of cilia and flagella is known as the?
questions.explanation: The axoneme is the microtubule core of a cilium or flagellum, usually in a 9 + 2 arrangement.

questions.text: Which of the following protein complexes is primarily responsible for the condensation of chromosomes during mitosis?
questions.explanation: Condensin coils and compacts chromosomes for mitosis. Cohesin holds sister chromatids together.

questions.text: Which organelle is primarily responsible for detoxifying harmful substances, such as drugs and alcohol, in a cell?
questions.explanation: Smooth ER carries the enzymes that detoxify drugs and alcohol, especially in liver cells.

questions.text: The kinetochore forms at the centromere of a chromosome. The centromere is also referred to as the?
questions.explanation: The centromere is the narrowed region of a chromosome, so it is called the primary constriction. The kinetochore forms on it.

questions.text: Which enzyme is specifically used to untangle and relieve the tension in coiled or supercoiled DNA during replication?
questions.explanation: Topoisomerase cuts and rejoins DNA to release supercoiling ahead of the replication fork. Helicase unwinds the strands.

questions.text: The Chromosomal Theory of Inheritance was independently proposed by?
questions.explanation: Walter Sutton and Theodor Boveri independently proposed in 1902–1903 that genes are carried on chromosomes.

questions.text: What are the DNA filaments called that condense and appear as distinct structures during cell division?
questions.explanation: Chromatin is the DNA and protein filament that condenses into visible chromosomes when a cell divides.

questions.text: The structural organization of DNA and histones that appears as beads on a string under a microscope is called?
questions.explanation: Nucleosomes strung along DNA give chromatin its beads-on-a-string look.

questions.text: Which of the following are examples of biological macromolecules?
options: Proteins, Nucleic acids, Carbohydrates, and Lipids
questions.explanation: The four classes of biological macromolecule are proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates and lipids. Glucose, amino acids and nucleotides are their building blocks.

questions.text: Microbodies primarily function in?
options: Specific metabolic reactions, such as detoxification and fat breakdown
Providing structural support to the cell wall
questions.explanation: Microbodies such as peroxisomes carry out specific metabolic reactions, including detoxification and breaking down fats.

questions.text: Which of the following processes takes place in plants but not in animals?
questions.explanation: Plants photosynthesise. Aerobic respiration, active transport and mitosis happen in both plants and animals.

questions.text: At what phase of mitosis do the sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles?
questions.explanation: In anaphase the sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.

questions.text: The process of pollination by insects is known as?
questions.explanation: Entomophily is pollination by insects. Anemophily is by wind, hydrophily by water and chiropterophily by bats.

questions.text: Parasitic nutrition is found in all of the following organisms except?
questions.explanation: Roundworms, tapeworms and liver flukes live inside a host and feed on it. A mosquito lives freely and only visits to take blood.

questions.text: What are the four main whorls that make up a complete flower?
questions.explanation: The four whorls are calyx (sepals), corolla (petals), androecium (stamens) and gynoecium (carpels).

questions.text: Plants that complete their life cycle in one growing season are called?
questions.explanation: Annuals germinate, flower, seed and die within one growing season.

questions.text: What is a major limitation or refutation of Lamarck’s Theory of Inheritance of Acquired Characteristics?
options: Acquired traits, such as a bodybuilder's muscles, cannot be passed to offspring
Giraffes' necks grew longer over time
Organisms do not change over time
DNA is only found in the nucleus
questions.explanation: Changes acquired during life, such as built-up muscles, do not alter the genes in gametes, so they are not passed on.

questions.text: The Plasma Membrane is primarily composed of which molecules?
questions.explanation: The plasma membrane is made of lipids (mainly phospholipids), proteins and some carbohydrates attached to them.

questions.text: The proteins that span across the entire lipid bilayer of the plasma membrane are known as?
questions.explanation: Integral proteins pass through the lipid bilayer. Peripheral proteins sit on its surface.

questions.text: Who was the first person to observe and name "cells" while looking at cork?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke named cells in 1665 after looking at cork.

questions.text: What is the primary difference between Chromoplasts and Leucoplasts?
options: Chromoplasts store pigments; Leucoplasts store starch/nutrients
Chromoplasts are for respiration; Leucoplasts are for photosynthesis
Chromoplasts are found in animals; Leucoplasts are found in plants
Chromoplasts store water; Leucoplasts store oils
questions.explanation: Chromoplasts hold coloured pigments. Leucoplasts are colourless and store starch, oil or protein.

questions.text: Which of the following cellular components lack a membrane?
options: Both the ribosomes and the nucleolus
questions.explanation: Neither ribosomes nor the nucleolus has a membrane. Mitochondria have two.

questions.text: How many pairs of sex chromosomes are found in a human cell?
questions.explanation: Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes: 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes.

questions.text: Which of the following best defines pollination?
options: The fusion of male and female gametes to form a zygote
The transfer of pollen grains from the anther of a stamen to the receptive stigma of a carpel
The dispersal of seeds away from the parent plant by wind or water
The process by which a seed begins to grow into a seedling
questions.explanation: Pollination is only the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma. Fusion of gametes is fertilization.

questions.text: Which of the following animals is not viviparous?
questions.explanation: Most snakes lay eggs. Apes, gorillas and cheetahs are mammals that bear live young.

questions.text: What is the outermost whorl of a flower, which is usually green and protects the flower during the bud stage?
questions.explanation: The calyx, made of sepals, is the outermost whorl and protects the bud.

questions.text: Mycoplasma organisms are generally smaller than typical bacteria.
questions.explanation: Mycoplasmas are among the smallest known cells, about 0.1–0.3 µm across, and have no cell wall.

questions.text: Which of the following is a type of protein found within the plasma membrane?
questions.explanation: Transmembrane proteins cross the plasma membrane. Tubulin and keratin belong to the cytoskeleton and ribophorins to the rough ER.

questions.text: Which histone protein is the most highly conserved and is therefore preferred for comparison across different eukaryotic species?
questions.explanation: Of these, H3 changes least between species. H3 and H4 are the most conserved histones.

questions.text: Which organelle is primarily responsible for the processing, packaging, and intracellular transport of proteins and lipids for secretion?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus processes and packages proteins and lipids for secretion.

questions.text: Sickle cell trait is best described as a?
questions.explanation: Sickle cell trait concerns how haemoglobin works in the blood, so it is classed as a physiological trait.

questions.text: A Test Cross is performed by crossing an individual with an unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive individual. If the resulting offspring show a 1:1 ratio of traits, the unknown genotype is?
questions.explanation: A heterozygote (Aa) crossed with aa gives half Aa and half aa, a 1:1 ratio. A homozygous dominant parent would give only dominant offspring.

questions.text: The process by which a new plant grows from a fragment or specialized reproductive structure of the parent plant is?
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation grows a new plant from a part of the parent, such as a stem, root or leaf.

questions.text: During the early stages of cell division, the genetic material condenses from a diffuse mass into visible thread-like structures called?
questions.explanation: Diffuse chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes early in cell division.

questions.text: An organism's behavior is typically influenced or determined by?
questions.explanation: Behaviour depends on both inherited genes and the environment.

questions.text: Algae grow and multiply rapidly in the presence of water and nutrients primarily through?
questions.explanation: With plenty of water and nutrients, algae break into fragments that each grow into a new individual.

questions.text: The primary method of asexual reproduction in bread molds is?
questions.explanation: Bread mould (Rhizopus) reproduces asexually by spores made in sporangia.

questions.text: Reproduction in plants that does not involve flowers, fruits, or seeds is known as?
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation uses roots, stems or leaves instead of flowers, fruits or seeds.

questions.text: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was the first to discover and describe little animals which he called?
questions.explanation: Leeuwenhoek called the microorganisms he saw animalcules, meaning little animals.

questions.text: What is the primary function of the cytosol?
options: To protect the cell from the external environment
To act as the site for many metabolic reactions and suspend organelles
To generate ATP via aerobic respiration
questions.explanation: Cytosol is the fluid where many metabolic reactions, such as glycolysis, happen and in which organelles are suspended.

questions.text: The part of the cell that consists of the jelly-like substance holding all the organelles in place is the?
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm is the jelly-like material that holds the organelles in place.

questions.text: Which organelle is specifically responsible for detoxifying metabolic waste and harmful substances?
questions.explanation: Peroxisomes break down toxic substances, using catalase to destroy hydrogen peroxide.

questions.text: The cell organelle containing oxidative/reducing enzymes responsible for the breakdown of long-chain fatty acids is the?
questions.explanation: Peroxisomes contain oxidative enzymes that break down long-chain fatty acids.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a process associated with sexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: Parthenocarpy is fruit forming without fertilization. Meiosis, gamete formation and fertilization are all steps of sexual reproduction.

questions.text: Which of the following concepts best represents the core of Darwin’s theory (Darwinism)?
questions.explanation: Darwin's theory centres on survival of the fittest. Use and disuse and acquired traits belong to Lamarck.

questions.text: In genetics, a trait that is expressed and masks the effect of another trait in a heterozygous individual is described as?
questions.explanation: A dominant trait shows in a heterozygote and masks the recessive one.

questions.text: Systematics is the study of the diversification of living forms. Which of the following is not a characteristic or goal of Systematics?
options: Covering and naming all known organisms
Classifying organisms based on shared traits
Focusing only on Classifying organisms based on relationship between them
questions.explanation: Systematics names, classifies and traces the evolution of organisms. It is not limited to classification.

questions.text: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther of one flower to the receptive stigma of another flower is known as?
questions.explanation: Moving pollen from one flower to the stigma of another is cross-pollination.

questions.text: The confusion or complexity in understanding animal diversity is often increased by the process of?
questions.explanation: Evolution keeps producing new forms, which makes animal diversity harder to sort out.

questions.text: Which of Mendel’s laws is demonstrated by a dihybrid cross resulting in a phenotypic ratio of 9:3:3:1?
questions.explanation: A 9:3:3:1 ratio appears because the two genes assort independently.

questions.text: What scientific discipline provides the system for organizing, naming, and recalling the roughly 1.5 million known species groups?
questions.explanation: Taxonomy is the science of naming, describing and organising species.

questions.text: The saying "Omnis cellula e cellula" emphasizes which biological concept?
options: Cells being created from inorganic matter
questions.explanation: "Omnis cellula e cellula" is Latin for "every cell comes from a cell". Virchow popularised it.

questions.text: The Tonoplast is a specialized membrane found surrounding which organelle?
questions.explanation: The tonoplast is the membrane around the large central vacuole of a plant cell.

questions.text: The fusion of the haploid nucleus of a sperm cell with the haploid nucleus of an egg cell results in a?
questions.explanation: Two haploid nuclei (n + n) fuse to give a diploid zygote (2n).

questions.text: The primary function of the large central vacuole in a plant cell is?
options: Storage of nutrients/waste and maintaining cell rigidity
questions.explanation: The central vacuole stores nutrients and waste, and its turgor pressure keeps the cell rigid.

questions.text: Viruses are generally smaller than?
questions.explanation: Most viruses are 20–300 nm, smaller than most bacteria but far larger than atoms and small molecules.

questions.text: Who is credited with coining the term "Chromosome" in 1888?
questions.explanation: Heinrich Wilhelm Waldeyer coined the word chromosome, "coloured body", in 1888.

questions.text: Which part of the cell acts as the primary boundary and facilitates the physical connection and communication between adjacent cells?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is the boundary of the cell and carries the proteins that connect it to its neighbours.

questions.text: Which organelle or structure is responsible for the organization and formation of spindle fibers during animal cell division?
questions.explanation: Centrioles organise the spindle fibres in animal cells.

questions.text: What is the typical size range for most eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Most eukaryotic cells are 10–100 µm. Prokaryotes are usually 1–10 µm.

questions.text: The pistil of a flower is composed of which three parts?
questions.explanation: A pistil is made of the stigma, style and ovary.

questions.text: The gene for color blindness is located on which chromosome?
questions.explanation: Colour blindness is X-linked. Males have only one X, so one faulty copy is enough.

questions.text: The total collection of all the different genes and alleles present in a breeding population is called the?
questions.explanation: The gene pool is all the alleles in a breeding population. A genome belongs to one organism.

questions.text: What is the primary function of the chloroplast in a plant cell?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are the site of photosynthesis.

questions.text: In the hierarchy of biological classification, which level is the most exclusive and contains only one type of organism?
questions.explanation: Species is the lowest rank and contains only one kind of organism.

questions.text: Which of the following is a primary function of lysosomes?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes that break down worn-out parts and waste inside the cell.

questions.text: How many pairs of autosomes are found in a normal human somatic cell?
questions.explanation: Humans have 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes.

questions.text: Polymerization is the chemical process of?
options: Breaking down large molecules into smaller units
The movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane
Combining small repeating units to form a large molecule
questions.explanation: Polymerization joins many small units (monomers) into one large molecule.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about chromosomes is true?
options: They are only found in the cytoplasm
The terminal ends of a chromosome are called telomeres
They are always X-shaped regardless of the cell cycle stage
questions.explanation: The ends of a chromosome are called telomeres. Chromosomes are in the nucleus, contain proteins, and are X-shaped only after replication.

questions.text: What is the core concept or main theory of Charles Darwin's evolutionary model?
questions.explanation: Darwin's main idea was natural selection.

questions.text: After fertilization, the ripened ovule develops into the?
questions.explanation: After fertilization the ovule becomes the seed and the ovary becomes the fruit.

questions.text: A fruit is botanically defined as a matured or ripened?
questions.explanation: A fruit is a ripened ovary.

questions.text: A new mutation can spread through a population and become more common primarily through the process of?
questions.explanation: A mutation spreads if it is favoured by natural selection or, by chance, through genetic drift.

questions.text: In a prokaryotic cell, the genetic material is not enclosed in a membrane but is found in a concentrated region called the?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic DNA lies in the nucleoid, a region with no membrane.

questions.text: At which phase of the cell cycle is the genetic material found in its uncondensed, thread-like form known as chromatin?
questions.explanation: During interphase DNA is uncondensed chromatin. It condenses from prophase.

questions.text: The beads-on-a-string structures found on the chromonemata are called?
questions.explanation: Chromomeres are the bead-like thickenings along the chromonemata.

questions.text: Systematics is best defined as the study of?
options: Grouping and naming organisms based on evolutionary trends
Grouping all animals and plants by size only
The study of cell division only
The study of chemical reactions in the cytosol
questions.explanation: Systematics groups and names organisms according to their evolutionary relationships.

questions.text: Eukaryotic cells are much larger than prokaryotic cells. They tackle the issue of slow diffusion through?
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic cells divide their interior into membrane-bound compartments, which shortens diffusion distances.

questions.text: What is primarily responsible for cell adhesion?
questions.explanation: Glycoproteins on the cell surface let cells recognise and stick to each other.

questions.text: What are the units of a ribosome in a Eukaryotic cell?
questions.explanation: The eukaryotic 80S ribosome has 60S and 40S subunits. Prokaryotic 70S ribosomes have 50S and 30S.

questions.text: In taxonomy, organisms are categorized based on strict rules. Which of the following is NOT a standard basis for grouping into a Domain?
questions.explanation: Organisms are grouped using properties, rules and principles. The period an organism lived in is not a basis for a domain.

questions.text: Which of the following combinations represents the three main types of plastids found in plants?
questions.explanation: The three main plastids are chloroplasts, chromoplasts and leucoplasts.

questions.text: The surface area to volume ratio of a cell decreases with?
questions.explanation: As a cell grows, volume rises faster than surface area, so the ratio falls.

questions.text: The chromatin that makes up chromosomes consists of?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are made of nucleic acid (DNA) bound to basic proteins, the histones.

questions.text: The budding form of reproduction is commonly found in which fungus?
questions.explanation: Yeast reproduces by budding. Conidia and sporangia are spore structures.

questions.text: When two or more organisms share the same limited resources in an environment, it is called?
questions.explanation: Organisms that need the same limited resource compete for it.

questions.text: Which part of the mitochondria is most closely associated with the enzymes for ATP production?
questions.explanation: Of these, the matrix is the part of the mitochondrion that holds enzymes feeding ATP production, such as those of the Krebs cycle. Thylakoids belong to chloroplasts.

questions.text: The Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) is primarily used for?
options: Synthesis and transport of proteins and lipids
questions.explanation: Rough ER makes and moves proteins, and smooth ER makes lipids.

questions.text: Genetic materials are encoded in?
questions.explanation: Genetic information is encoded in DNA.

questions.text: The phenotypic ratio of a Mendelian monohybrid cross is?
questions.explanation: A monohybrid cross of two heterozygotes gives 3 dominant to 1 recessive. 1:2:1 is the genotypic ratio.

questions.text: How many pairs of chromosomes are in a normal human cell?
questions.explanation: A normal human body cell has 46 chromosomes, which is 23 pairs.

questions.text: Which organelle is termed the "suicidal bag"?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are called suicidal bags because their enzymes can digest the whole cell if they burst.

questions.text: Why do animal vacuoles maintain their small size compared to plant vacuoles?
options: Animals do not need to store water
They are used for temporary storage rather than structural support
Animal cells have a cell wall that limits size
They are only present during cell division
questions.explanation: Animal vacuoles are small because they only store things temporarily. Plant vacuoles also give structural support.

questions.text: Animals are not diverse in terms of their?
questions.explanation: Animals vary in habitat, symmetry and reproduction, but all of them are heterotrophs.

questions.text: A macromolecule can be described as?
questions.explanation: A macromolecule is a large molecule, usually a polymer of smaller units.

questions.text: Which histone protein is responsible for clamping or compacting the DNA the most by securing the entry/exit of the DNA around the core?
questions.explanation: H1 is the linker histone. It clamps the DNA where it enters and leaves the nucleosome core.
